problem: Multi-task training of retrieval-augmented generation models for knowledge-intensive tasks faces challenges due to coverage sparsity of relevance judgements, noisy labels from heuristic mappings in benchmarks like KILT, and severe task imbalances (p.1-2).
methodology: The authors propose a confidence-based relevance-label sampling strategy to filter out training examples where no knowledge item is sufficiently relevant (threshold t > 0 using BLEU score mapping), alongside downsampling oversized tasks to 200K examples for balanced multi-task training of a Fusion-in-Decoder (FiD) generator (p.1-3). They also propose an alternative passage aggregation strategy (Alt-200) that chunks text up to 200 words without breaking paragraphs (p.3), and they evaluate scaling the generator backbone from T5-Base to T5-Large and T5-XL (p.2, 4).
dataset: Seven combined tasks of the KILT benchmark spanning open domain QA, slot filling, fact verification, and dialogue: HotpotQA, TriviaQA, Natural Questions (NQ), T-REx, Zero Shot RE (zsRE), FEVER, and Wizard of Wikipedia (WoW) (p.1, 3).
results: The training strategy significantly improves effectiveness on strongly imbalanced datasets, yielding gains of +12.7 EM on TriviaQA and +4.9 Accuracy on T-REx, alongside smaller significant gains on NQ and zsRE (p.2, 4). Scaling the T5 backbone up to T5-XL achieves state-of-the-art results on five out of seven KILT tasks on the official leaderboard: NQ, TriviaQA, FEVER, zsRE, and WoW (p.2, 4).
key_findings: Filtering training data using relevance-label confidence reduces training set size by 25% while substantially improving performance on imbalanced tasks and scaling well with increased model capacity (p.2, 4). Multi-task training with a single model is shown to be a viable, strong baseline approach without requiring end-to-end retriever training, multiple training loops, or knowledge distillation (p.4).
limitations: The approach comes in second place on HotpotQA and T-REx on the leaderboard, which may be attributable to a handicapped zero-shot retriever or downsampling of the T-REx training data (p.4). Additionally, the retriever module is fixed rather than jointly trained (p.4).
title: Multi-Task Retrieval-Augmented Text Generation with Relevance Sampling
